title: Parts for the Crusher
summary: The Crusher's new cutting head has arrived from the smiths — gyro-stabilised, ceramic-collared, and worth a season of leverage. It must cross ninety metres of the most obstacle-dense real estate on Kessa-9 on courier suspension, down the processional route, without one hard bounce. The Yards will line the rope and grade your line out loud.

objectives.label: Lift the cutting head from its cradle at Pyke's office
Take the processional under the yard gate — slowly; the rope line is judging
Set the head into the Crusher's feed cradle

offer.text: Courier. The Crusher's dental work is in from the smiths — one gyro-stabilised cutting head, ceramic collar, cost me a season of leverage and three favors I was saving for funerals. It crosses the yard on *your* suspension, because hauler suspension is an insult to ceramics.

Plain speaking, since Boss is being delicate: the collar cracks, we eat a season of spare teeth, metaphorically, which is the only way you'd want to. Between the office and the hopper lies an open-air museum of things you will want to hit. Decline.
Ninety metres of junkyard, carrying the most expensive part of the junkyard-eater, past an audience of people who strip machines professionally. Sure. This is fine.

accept.text: Processional route: out my door, under the yard gate, straight-ish to the cradle. Above walking pace is theatre we cannot afford. Vertex's people will applaud a clean line. They've graded couriers out loud since before the bridge burned.

Yards band for the courier: ode in progress, title *The Head That Crossed the Yard*. Currently twelve lines long, duck — the precise length of the journey if you bounce it. Ride so I have to cut verses.
Ketch here. Fragile jobs are boring by *specification*. Boring is the luxury good we're selling today. Keep your hover height humble and let the Cargo Shield Drink do its job.

complete.text: Intact. Hear that collar sing in the cradle? That's a season of leverage coming home in tune. Payment posted — and courier, the rope line heard you didn't bounce. That *spends* in the Yards.

The ode comes in at four lines, duck. Four. You understand what you've cost me. *She crossed like morning crosses salt — unhurried — and the collar sang her name in ceramic.* Well. Some of it was worth keeping.
First bite at dusk, if you want to hear her purr. Bring ear protection and a respect you didn't arrive with. Both are standard kit now.
